sections.h2: Who files the deed after an Ionia County home sale?
sections.html:
The Ionia County Register of Deeds files it. That office keeps the land records for the whole county, and a sale becomes public only once the deed is stamped, indexed and filed there. Staff will not help you draft or repair paperwork, so the papers should arrive complete, drafted by a lawyer or the closing company.

Land area in Ionia County is roughly 571 square miles. The seat is the city of Ionia, and the county counts as part of the Grand Rapids-Kentwood metro area. Filing can happen at the counter, through the mail, or through an approved electronic provider. Counter filings are handed back on the spot. Mailed packets come back only if you include a self-addressed return envelope, and anything sent without one is held 90 days. For questions, call (616) 527-5320 or write deeds@ioniacounty.org.

sections.h2: What will the Ionia County deed filing cost me?
sections.html:
Thirty dollars covers each document, however long. Payment can be cash, check or card, and card payments add a service fee that depends on the amount. One check can cover the filing charge and both transfer taxes.

Ionia County Register of Deeds charges
ItemAmount
Filing a deed or mortgage$30.00 per document
Document that assigns or discharges several instruments$3.00 for each one past the first
Treasurer tax certification (warranty deeds, land contracts)$5.00
Name lookup by staff$5.00
Photocopies$1.00 a page
Certifying a copy$5.00 added

Source: Ionia County Register of Deeds pages on fees and on searching and copies.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured on an Ionia County sale?
sections.html:
Ionia County publishes two rates that apply to a deed conveying real estate for money. The state takes $3.75 for every $500 of price, counting any partial $500 as a full one, and the county takes $0.55 on the same basis. A $200,000 price therefore produces $1,500 state tax and $220 county tax, $1,720 combined. That is simple arithmetic on the posted rates; your closing agent will confirm the final number.

Any claimed exemption goes in writing on the deed itself. The two Michigan statutes do not match, and the gap matters for family transfers:

  • MCL 207.526 (state tax) exempts a deed from a parent or grandparent to a child, stepchild or grandchild, along with foreclosure deeds and deeds in place of foreclosure.
  • MCL 207.505 (county tax) exempts instruments valued under $100, security instruments, leases, and court orders that name no price, and it omits the child and grandchild category.
  • Both statutes exempt a land contract until the full contract price has been paid and title passes.

So a gift deed to a daughter can owe county tax while owing nothing to the state. Ask the office how your transfer is classified before you sign.

sections.h2: Which sales need a treasurer certification first?
sections.html:
Warranty deeds, any deed with a covenant of warranty, land contracts, and assignments of land contracts must carry a Tax Certification from the Ionia County Treasurer. The $5 charge can sit on the same check as the filing charge. A quitclaim deed has no warranty covenant, so it usually avoids this step, and the Register of Deeds can say whether yours does.

If back taxes are owed on the parcel, raise it with your closing agent early, because the certification is part of the package that gets filed. Ask the County Treasurer what the office requires before it will issue one.

sections.h2: Why would the office send my deed back?
sections.html:
Clerks check each document against Michigan's recording statute, MCL 565.201 and related sections. A deed that misses a rule comes back, and a closing can stall for days. The county's own checklist covers the usual trouble spots:

  • Signatures are originals in dark ink, black or dark blue, with each name printed below.
  • The notary block repeats the same printed names, and the notary's name sits on the page that holds the notary signature.
  • The buyer's mailing address appears, as does the drafter's name and address as well.
  • Page one leaves a 2 1/2 inch blank band at the top, with half an inch clear on the remaining edges.
  • The first printed line names the one recordable event the paper covers.
  • Print is black, 10 point or larger, on white stock of at least 20 pound weight, in letter or legal size.
  • A deed to a surviving owner needs a certified death certificate recorded with it or earlier.
  • The full property value is stated on the deed, or a transfer tax valuation affidavit goes with it.

sections.h2: Can I look up Ionia County land records myself?
sections.html:
Yes. Public workstations in the office let you search by grantor or grantee for free, with copies at $1 a page. Searching those machines by legal description or parcel number runs $1 per minute. If you ask staff to find your last deed, the fee is $5 plus copies, and the lookup works by name rather than by property.

Remote searching comes in two forms. Tapestry charges $8.95 per search and suits a single visit. Laredo bills monthly and fits agents, investors and anyone searching often; call the office to open an account. If either service gives you trouble, the county asks that you contact the vendor's support team (Fidlar) first and the Ionia filing counter after that. A title company search digs deeper than either tool when you need the full ownership chain behind your house.

sections.h2: How do Ionia County housing numbers compare for a seller?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts puts the population at 66,557 in July 2025, slightly under the April 2020 count of 66,804. About 77.3 percent of households own, with a typical owned home worth $198,500 (2020 to 2024 survey years). Typical household income of $75,611 is the highest among the four Michigan counties researched alongside this one.

Commuters average 27.1 minutes each way to work, the longest of those four counties, which fits a county that feeds the Grand Rapids job market. Rent runs $884 a month at the median, and builders pulled only 100 permits in 2025. Resale houses supply most of what buyers see, and your listing joins that pool.

sections.h2: Will the next property tax bill look different after I sell?
sections.html:
A transfer of ownership uncaps taxable value. Under Proposal A, the new figure takes effect in the calendar year after the transfer, so the buyer's bill can climb toward the assessed value. Michigan Treasury posts the Property Transfer Affidavit, Form 2766, which the buyer files with the local assessor. Ask the assessor for your city or township about the filing deadline.

Transfers listed in section 211.27a(7) of the General Property Tax Act do not uncap. Assessment is a local job in Michigan, handled by the city or township where the house stands, so the assessor there is the person to call about taxable value. Current bills come from that same local unit, and the County Treasurer takes over delinquent ones.

faqs.q: Does Ionia County bill by page count?
faqs.a: No. Each document costs $30 to file. Documents that assign or discharge several instruments add $3 for each extra one.

faqs.q: May I email a deed to the Ionia County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: No. Email filings are refused. Electronic recording runs through accredited servicers named on the county page: Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, EPN and CSC. Only a scanned original signed document is accepted.

faqs.q: Who covers transfer tax in Ionia County?
faqs.a: Neither buyer nor seller is named on the county page. Payment comes with the deed at filing, so read your purchase agreement and watch the settlement statement for the amount.

faqs.q: Will paying off my mortgage give me a new deed?
faqs.a: No. Your lender files a discharge of mortgage, which carries the same $30 filing charge, and your original deed remains the proof of ownership.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim to a relative taxed in Ionia County?
faqs.a: It may be taxed by the county. The state list exempts gifts to a child or grandchild, and the county list leaves them out. The deed has to state the exemption, so ask the office first.
